People HR is a cloud-based human resource management system that provides tools for managing employee records, holidays, salaries, vacancies, applicants, appraisals, and custom screens. The Ballerina ballerinax/peoplehr connector (v2.2.1) provides programmatic access to the People HR REST API (v3.1), enabling you to integrate People HR data into your Ballerina integration flows.

Full employee lifecycle management: create, retrieve, update, and mark employees as leavers Holiday management: add, retrieve, and delete employee holiday records Salary detail retrieval with optional history Vacancy and applicant management: create vacancies, list all vacancies, create applicants, upload documents, and check for duplicates Custom screen transaction support: add, update, delete, and retrieve employee custom screen details Appraisal detail retrieval by employee ID or appraisal ID Saved query execution by query name for flexible data retrieval Authentication verification for validating user credentials

Actions are operations you invoke on People HR from your integration, including managing employees, holidays, salaries, vacancies, applicants, custom screens, and more. The People HR connector exposes actions through a single client: Client Actions Client Employee CRUD, holiday management, salary details, vacancy and applicant management, custom screens, appraisals, queries, authentication See the Action Reference for the full list of operations, parameters, and sample code for each client.

Setup Guide: This guide walks you through creating a People HR account and obtaining the API key required to use the People HR connector. Action Reference: Full reference for all clients: operations, parameters, return types, and sample code. Example: Learn how to build and configure an integration using the People HR connector, including connection setup, operation configuration, and execution flow.

This guide walks you through getting the necessary details from SAP SuccessFactors so that the connector can authenticate and communicate with your Employee Central instance. This connector supports two authentication methods: Basic Authentication and OAuth 2.0 SAML Bearer.

If you already have a username and password for this integration to work, you can use those directly. If you'd rather create a new account with narrowed scope for this integration, follow these steps: Sign in to your SAP SuccessFactors instance as an administrator. Navigate to Admin Center > Add New Employee and create a new user account for this integration. Navigate to Admin Center > Manage Permission Roles, create a role scoped to only the permissions this integration needs, and grant it to the new user. Navigate to Admin Center > Reset User Password and set a password for the new user account. In either case, you will also need the API server hostname for your SuccessFactors region, for example, api12.successfactors.eu. The complete list of API server hostnames by region is available in the SAP SuccessFactors API documentation.

Generate an RSA key pair and a matching X.509 certificate. If you don't already have one, generate a self-signed pair with OpenSSL: openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout private_key.pem -out certificate.pem -days 365 -nodes -subj "/CN=YourAppName" private_key.pem is secret - it never leaves your machine or gets uploaded anywhere. Only certificate.pem is registered with SAP.
documents.s: Step 1: Generate a key pair and certificate

documents.t: Sign in to your SAP SuccessFactors instance as an administrator. Search for Manage OAuth2 Client Applications in Admin Center's action search, or navigate to it directly under Admin Center > Company Settings. Choose Register Client Application and provide the following information: Field Description Application Name A name to identify this integration Description An optional description X.509 Certificate The contents of certificate.pem as a single continuous base64 string, with the -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- / -----END CERTIFICATE----- lines and line breaks removed. Produce this with awk '/BEGIN CERTIFICATE/{flag=1;next}/END CERTIFICATE/{flag=0}flag' certificate.pem | tr -d '\n' and paste the single line of output it prints. Choose Register to save the application.
documents.s: Step 2: Register an OAuth2 client application

documents.t: After registering, open the application (choose View from the application list) to find the Company ID and the API Key SAP assigned to it. You now have everything the connector's SAML Bearer configuration needs: the API Key, the Company ID, the username to authenticate as, your private_key.pem and certificate.pem files, and the OAuth2 token endpoint (typically https://<admin-center-host>/oauth/token).

This guide walks you through getting the necessary details from SAP SuccessFactors so that the connector can authenticate and communicate with your Employee Central instance. This connector supports two authentication methods: Basic Authentication and OAuth 2.0 SAML Bearer.

If you already have a username and password for this integration to work, you can use those directly. If you'd rather create a new account with narrowed scope for this integration, follow these steps: Sign in to your SAP SuccessFactors instance as an administrator. Navigate to Admin Center > Add New Employee and create a new user account for this integration. Navigate to Admin Center > Manage Permission Roles, create a role scoped to only the permissions this integration needs, and grant it to the new user. Navigate to Admin Center > Reset User Password and set a password for the new user account. In either case, you will also need the API server hostname for your SuccessFactors region, for example, api12.successfactors.eu. The complete list of API server hostnames by region is available in the SAP SuccessFactors API documentation.

Generate an RSA key pair and a matching X.509 certificate. If you don't already have one, generate a self-signed pair with OpenSSL: openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout private_key.pem -out certificate.pem -days 365 -nodes -subj "/CN=YourAppName" private_key.pem is secret - it never leaves your machine or gets uploaded anywhere. Only certificate.pem is registered with SAP.
documents.s: Step 1: Generate a key pair and certificate

documents.t: Sign in to your SAP SuccessFactors instance as an administrator. Search for Manage OAuth2 Client Applications in Admin Center's action search, or navigate to it directly under Admin Center > Company Settings. Choose Register Client Application and provide the following information: Field Description Application Name A name to identify this integration Description An optional description X.509 Certificate The contents of certificate.pem as a single continuous base64 string, with the -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- / -----END CERTIFICATE----- lines and line breaks removed. Produce this with awk '/BEGIN CERTIFICATE/{flag=1;next}/END CERTIFICATE/{flag=0}flag' certificate.pem | tr -d '\n' and paste the single line of output it prints. Choose Register to save the application.
documents.s: Step 2: Register an OAuth2 client application

documents.t: After registering, open the application (choose View from the application list) to find the Company ID and the API Key SAP assigned to it. You now have everything the connector's SAML Bearer configuration needs: the API Key, the Company ID, the username to authenticate as, your private_key.pem and certificate.pem files, and the OAuth2 token endpoint (typically https://<admin-center-host>/oauth/token).

SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central is a comprehensive human capital management solution that helps organizations manage their workforce effectively. It provides a unified platform for HR processes including employee data management, organizational structures, and employment lifecycle management. WSO2 SAP Successfactors Compensation Information provides a way to interact with the SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central APIs. The service allows to manage employee compensation data, salary information, and pay components.

This guide walks you through getting the necessary details from SAP SuccessFactors so that the connector can authenticate and communicate with your Employee Central instance. This connector supports two authentication methods: Basic Authentication and OAuth 2.0 SAML Bearer.

If you already have a username and password for this integration to work, you can use those directly. If you'd rather create a new account with narrowed scope for this integration, follow these steps: Sign in to your SAP SuccessFactors instance as an administrator. Navigate to Admin Center > Add New Employee and create a new user account for this integration. Navigate to Admin Center > Manage Permission Roles, create a role scoped to only the permissions this integration needs, and grant it to the new user. Navigate to Admin Center > Reset User Password and set a password for the new user account. In either case, you will also need the API server hostname for your SuccessFactors region, for example, api12.successfactors.eu. The complete list of API server hostnames by region is available in the SAP SuccessFactors API documentation.

Generate an RSA key pair and a matching X.509 certificate. If you don't already have one, generate a self-signed pair with OpenSSL: openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout private_key.pem -out certificate.pem -days 365 -nodes -subj "/CN=YourAppName" private_key.pem is secret - it never leaves your machine or gets uploaded anywhere. Only certificate.pem is registered with SAP.
documents.s: Step 1: Generate a key pair and certificate

documents.t: Sign in to your SAP SuccessFactors instance as an administrator. Search for Manage OAuth2 Client Applications in Admin Center's action search, or navigate to it directly under Admin Center > Company Settings. Choose Register Client Application and provide the following information: Field Description Application Name A name to identify this integration Description An optional description X.509 Certificate The contents of certificate.pem as a single continuous base64 string, with the -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- / -----END CERTIFICATE----- lines and line breaks removed. Produce this with awk '/BEGIN CERTIFICATE/{flag=1;next}/END CERTIFICATE/{flag=0}flag' certificate.pem | tr -d '\n' and paste the single line of output it prints. Choose Register to save the application.
documents.s: Step 2: Register an OAuth2 client application

documents.t: After registering, open the application (choose View from the application list) to find the Company ID and the API Key SAP assigned to it. You now have everything the connector's SAML Bearer configuration needs: the API Key, the Company ID, the username to authenticate as, your private_key.pem and certificate.pem files, and the OAuth2 token endpoint (typically https://<admin-center-host>/oauth/token).

This guide walks you through getting the necessary details from SAP SuccessFactors so that the connector can authenticate and communicate with your Employee Central instance. This connector supports two authentication methods: Basic Authentication and OAuth 2.0 SAML Bearer.

If you already have a username and password for this integration to work, you can use those directly. If you'd rather create a new account with narrowed scope for this integration, follow these steps: Sign in to your SAP SuccessFactors instance as an administrator. Navigate to Admin Center > Add New Employee and create a new user account for this integration. Navigate to Admin Center > Manage Permission Roles, create a role scoped to only the permissions this integration needs, and grant it to the new user. Navigate to Admin Center > Reset User Password and set a password for the new user account. In either case, you will also need the API server hostname for your SuccessFactors region, for example, api12.successfactors.eu. The complete list of API server hostnames by region is available in the SAP SuccessFactors API documentation.

Generate an RSA key pair and a matching X.509 certificate. If you don't already have one, generate a self-signed pair with OpenSSL: openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout private_key.pem -out certificate.pem -days 365 -nodes -subj "/CN=YourAppName" private_key.pem is secret - it never leaves your machine or gets uploaded anywhere. Only certificate.pem is registered with SAP.
documents.s: Step 1: Generate a key pair and certificate

documents.t: Sign in to your SAP SuccessFactors instance as an administrator. Search for Manage OAuth2 Client Applications in Admin Center's action search, or navigate to it directly under Admin Center > Company Settings. Choose Register Client Application and provide the following information: Field Description Application Name A name to identify this integration Description An optional description X.509 Certificate The contents of certificate.pem as a single continuous base64 string, with the -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- / -----END CERTIFICATE----- lines and line breaks removed. Produce this with awk '/BEGIN CERTIFICATE/{flag=1;next}/END CERTIFICATE/{flag=0}flag' certificate.pem | tr -d '\n' and paste the single line of output it prints. Choose Register to save the application.
documents.s: Step 2: Register an OAuth2 client application

documents.t: After registering, open the application (choose View from the application list) to find the Company ID and the API Key SAP assigned to it. You now have everything the connector's SAML Bearer configuration needs: the API Key, the Company ID, the username to authenticate as, your private_key.pem and certificate.pem files, and the OAuth2 token endpoint (typically https://<admin-center-host>/oauth/token).

Build an integration that connects to SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central and retrieves employee payroll run result item records through the SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central Payroll connector. The integration exposes an automation entry point that calls the operation and stores the result in a variable you can process further. Operations used: List Employee Payroll Run Results Itemss : Queries the EmployeePayrollRunResultsItems collection and returns a page of entities, optionally filtered, sorted, and paged through OData query options.
Access to a SAP SuccessFactors OData API server (see the setup guide) A company ID, username, and password, or OAuth 2.0 credentials
New to WSO2 Integrator? Follow the Create a New Integration guide to set up your integration first, then return here to add the connector.
documents.s: Setting up the SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central Payroll integration

documents.t: Select Add Artifact. Select Connection to open the connector search palette.
Enter ecemployeecentralpayroll in the search field. Select the Ecemployeecentralpayroll connector card.
documents.s: Step 2: Select the SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central Payroll connector

documents.t: Bind every required connection field to a configurable variable. Config : Expression containing the auth credentials for the SAP SuccessFactors OData server — bind username to a sfUsername configurable variable and password to a sfPassword configurable variable. Hostname : The SAP SuccessFactors OData API server hostname — bind to a sfHostname configurable variable.
documents.s: Step 3: Bind the connection parameters to configurable variables

documents.t: Select Save Connection and verify that ecemployeecentralpayrollClient appears in the Connections section.

Select Configurations at the bottom of the project tree under Data Mappers. Enter a value for each configurable listed below before you run the integration. sfUsername (configurable string) : The SAP SuccessFactors login username, formatted as <username>@<companyID>. sfPassword (configurable string) : The SAP SuccessFactors login password. sfHostname (configurable string) : The SAP SuccessFactors OData API server hostname, for example api68sales.successfactors.com.
documents.s: Step 5: Set actual values for your configurables

documents.t: Select Add Artifact. Select Automation. Select Create to accept the default settings.
documents.s: Step 6: Add an automation entry point

documents.t: Select the + icon between Start and Error Handler. Expand ecemployeecentralpayrollClient to display its operations. Select List Employee Payroll Run Results Itemss. The operation has no required parameters, so review the auto-generated result variable. Result : Name of the variable that stores the returned EmployeePayrollRunResultsItems records — leave the default value, ecemployeecentralpayrollWrapper. Select Save. The operation step appears in the automation flow between Start and Error Handler.
documents.s: Step 7: Expand the connection and configure the List Employee Payroll Run Results Itemss operation

Build an integration that connects to SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central and retrieves background community records through the SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central Employee Profile connector. The integration exposes an automation entry point that calls the operation and stores the result in a variable you can process further. Operations used: List Background Communities : Queries the Background_Community collection and returns a page of entities, optionally filtered, sorted, and paged through OData query options.
Access to a SAP SuccessFactors OData API server (see the setup guide) A company ID, username, and password, or OAuth 2.0 credentials
New to WSO2 Integrator? Follow the Create a New Integration guide to set up your integration first, then return here to add the connector.
documents.s: Setting up the SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central Employee Profile integration

documents.t: Select Add Artifact. Select Connection to open the connector search palette.
Enter ecemployeeprofile in the search field. Select the Ecemployeeprofile connector card.
documents.s: Step 2: Select the SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central Employee Profile connector

documents.t: Bind every required connection field to a configurable variable. Config : Expression containing the auth credentials for the SAP SuccessFactors OData server — bind username to a sfUsername configurable variable and password to a sfPassword configurable variable. Hostname : The SAP SuccessFactors OData API server hostname — bind to a sfHostname configurable variable.
documents.s: Step 3: Bind the connection parameters to configurable variables

documents.t: Select Save Connection and verify that ecemployeeprofileClient appears in the Connections section.

Select Configurations at the bottom of the project tree under Data Mappers. Enter a value for each configurable listed below before you run the integration. sfUsername (configurable string) : The SAP SuccessFactors login username, formatted as <username>@<companyID>. sfPassword (configurable string) : The SAP SuccessFactors login password. sfHostname (configurable string) : The SAP SuccessFactors OData API server hostname, for example api68sales.successfactors.com.
documents.s: Step 5: Set actual values for your configurables

documents.t: Select Add Artifact. Select Automation. Select Create to accept the default settings.
documents.s: Step 6: Add an automation entry point

documents.t: Select the + icon between Start and Error Handler. Expand ecemployeeprofileClient to display its operations. Select List Background Communities. The operation has no required parameters, so review the auto-generated result variable. Result : Name of the variable that stores the returned Background_Community records — leave the default value, ecemployeeprofileWrapper. Select Save. The operation step appears in the automation flow between Start and Error Handler.

SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central is a comprehensive human capital management solution that helps organizations manage their workforce effectively. It provides a unified platform for HR processes including employee data management, organizational structures, and employment lifecycle management. WSO2 SAP Successfactors Employee Profile provides a way to interact with the SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central APIs. The service allows to maintain the general background information of an employee, including education and outside work experiences.

documents.t: Manage employee profile information including personal details Access education background and work experience records Query background information across multiple categories

This guide walks you through getting the necessary details from SAP SuccessFactors so that the connector can authenticate and communicate with your Employee Central instance. This connector supports two authentication methods: Basic Authentication and OAuth 2.0 SAML Bearer.

If you already have a username and password for this integration to work, you can use those directly. If you'd rather create a new account with narrowed scope for this integration, follow these steps: Sign in to your SAP SuccessFactors instance as an administrator. Navigate to Admin Center > Add New Employee and create a new user account for this integration. Navigate to Admin Center > Manage Permission Roles, create a role scoped to only the permissions this integration needs, and grant it to the new user. Navigate to Admin Center > Reset User Password and set a password for the new user account. In either case, you will also need the API server hostname for your SuccessFactors region, for example, api12.successfactors.eu. The complete list of API server hostnames by region is available in the SAP SuccessFactors API documentation.

Generate an RSA key pair and a matching X.509 certificate. If you don't already have one, generate a self-signed pair with OpenSSL: openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout private_key.pem -out certificate.pem -days 365 -nodes -subj "/CN=YourAppName" private_key.pem is secret - it never leaves your machine or gets uploaded anywhere. Only certificate.pem is registered with SAP.
documents.s: Step 1: Generate a key pair and certificate

documents.t: Sign in to your SAP SuccessFactors instance as an administrator. Search for Manage OAuth2 Client Applications in Admin Center's action search, or navigate to it directly under Admin Center > Company Settings. Choose Register Client Application and provide the following information: Field Description Application Name A name to identify this integration Description An optional description X.509 Certificate The contents of certificate.pem as a single continuous base64 string, with the -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- / -----END CERTIFICATE----- lines and line breaks removed. Produce this with awk '/BEGIN CERTIFICATE/{flag=1;next}/END CERTIFICATE/{flag=0}flag' certificate.pem | tr -d '\n' and paste the single line of output it prints. Choose Register to save the application.
documents.s: Step 2: Register an OAuth2 client application

documents.t: After registering, open the application (choose View from the application list) to find the Company ID and the API Key SAP assigned to it. You now have everything the connector's SAML Bearer configuration needs: the API Key, the Company ID, the username to authenticate as, your private_key.pem and certificate.pem files, and the OAuth2 token endpoint (typically https://<admin-center-host>/oauth/token).
Action Reference - Available operations

The ballerinax/sap.successfactors.ecemploymentinformation package exposes the following clients: Available clients: Client Purpose Client Manages ecemploymentinformation objects: EmpBeneficiary, EmpEmployment, EmpEmploymentTermination, EmpPensionPayout, EmpWorkPermit, EmpJobRelationships, EmpJob, PersonEmpTerminationInfo…, over the SAP SuccessFactors OData v2 API.
You can use these APIs to access the employment related information, including job information, employment termination, and work permit.

ConnectionConfig​ Provides a set of configurations for controlling the behaviours when communicating with the SAP SuccessFactors OData endpoint. Passed as the argument to the client initializer. Field Type Default Description auth http:CredentialsConfig Required Configurations related to client authentication httpVersion http:HttpVersion See default The HTTP version understood by the client http1Settings http:ClientHttp1Settings See default Configurations related to HTTP/1.x protocol http2Settings http:ClientHttp2Settings See default Configurations related to HTTP/2 protocol timeout decimal See default The maximum time to wait (in seconds) for a response before closing the connection forwarded string See default The choice of setting forwarded/x-forwarded header followRedirects http:FollowRedirects Optional Configurations associated with Redirection poolConfig http:PoolConfiguration Optional Configurations associated with request pooling cache http:CacheConfig See default HTTP caching related configurations compression http:Compression See default Specifies the way of handling compression (accept-encoding) header circuitBreaker http:CircuitBreakerConfig Optional Configurations associated with the behaviour of the Circuit Breaker retryConfig http:RetryConfig Optional Configurations associated with retrying cookieConfig http:CookieConfig Optional Configurations associated with cookies responseLimits http:ResponseLimitConfigs See default Configurations associated with inbound response size limits secureSocket http:ClientSecureSocket Optional SSL/TLS-related options proxy http:ProxyConfig Optional Proxy server related options socketConfig http:ClientSocketConfig See default Provides settings related to client socket configuration validation boolean See default Enables the inbound payload validation functionality which provided by the constraint package. Enabled by default laxDataBinding boolean See default Enables relaxed data binding on the client side. When enabled, nil values are treated as optional, and absent fields are handled as nilable types. Enabled by default. The client also accepts a hostname string parameter (the SAP SuccessFactors API server host) and an optional port (defaults to 443).

import ballerinax/sap.successfactors.ecemploymentinformation; configurable string hostname = ?; configurable string username = ?; configurable string password = ?; ecemploymentinformation:Client client = check new ( { auth: { username, password } }, hostname );

Build an integration that connects to SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central and retrieves employee employment records through the SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central Employment Information connector. The integration exposes an automation entry point that calls the operation and stores the result in a variable you can process further. Operations used: List Emp Employments : Queries the EmpEmployment collection and returns a page of entities, optionally filtered, sorted, and paged through OData query options.
Access to a SAP SuccessFactors OData API server (see the setup guide) A company ID, username, and password, or OAuth 2.0 credentials
New to WSO2 Integrator? Follow the Create a New Integration guide to set up your integration first, then return here to add the connector.
documents.s: Setting up the SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central Employment Information integration

documents.t: Select Add Artifact. Select Connection to open the connector search palette.
Enter ecemploymentinformation in the search field. Select the Ecemploymentinformation connector card.
documents.s: Step 2: Select the SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central Employment Information connector

documents.t: Bind every required connection field to a configurable variable. Config : Expression containing the auth credentials for the SAP SuccessFactors OData server — bind username to a sfUsername configurable variable and password to a sfPassword configurable variable. Hostname : The SAP SuccessFactors OData API server hostname — bind to a sfHostname configurable variable.
documents.s: Step 3: Bind the connection parameters to configurable variables

documents.t: Select Save Connection and verify that ecemploymentinformationClient appears in the Connections section.

Select Configurations at the bottom of the project tree under Data Mappers. Enter a value for each configurable listed below before you run the integration. sfUsername (configurable string) : The SAP SuccessFactors login username, formatted as <username>@<companyID>. sfPassword (configurable string) : The SAP SuccessFactors login password. sfHostname (configurable string) : The SAP SuccessFactors OData API server hostname, for example api68sales.successfactors.com.
documents.s: Step 5: Set actual values for your configurables

documents.t: Select Add Artifact. Select Automation. Select Create to accept the default settings.
documents.s: Step 6: Add an automation entry point

documents.t: Select the + icon between Start and Error Handler. Expand ecemploymentinformationClient to display its operations. Select List Emp Employments. The operation has no required parameters, so review the auto-generated result variable. Result : Name of the variable that stores the returned EmpEmployment records — leave the default value, ecemploymentinformationWrapper1. Select Save. The operation step appears in the automation flow between Start and Error Handler.

SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central is a comprehensive human capital management solution that helps organizations manage their workforce effectively. It provides a unified platform for HR processes including employee data management, organizational structures, and employment lifecycle management. WSO2 SAP Successfactors Employment Information provides a way to interact with the SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central APIs. The service allows to access employment related information, including job information, employment termination, and work permit.

This guide walks you through getting the necessary details from SAP SuccessFactors so that the connector can authenticate and communicate with your Employee Central instance. This connector supports two authentication methods: Basic Authentication and OAuth 2.0 SAML Bearer.

If you already have a username and password for this integration to work, you can use those directly. If you'd rather create a new account with narrowed scope for this integration, follow these steps: Sign in to your SAP SuccessFactors instance as an administrator. Navigate to Admin Center > Add New Employee and create a new user account for this integration. Navigate to Admin Center > Manage Permission Roles, create a role scoped to only the permissions this integration needs, and grant it to the new user. Navigate to Admin Center > Reset User Password and set a password for the new user account. In either case, you will also need the API server hostname for your SuccessFactors region, for example, api12.successfactors.eu. The complete list of API server hostnames by region is available in the SAP SuccessFactors API documentation.

Generate an RSA key pair and a matching X.509 certificate. If you don't already have one, generate a self-signed pair with OpenSSL: openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout private_key.pem -out certificate.pem -days 365 -nodes -subj "/CN=YourAppName" private_key.pem is secret - it never leaves your machine or gets uploaded anywhere. Only certificate.pem is registered with SAP.
documents.s: Step 1: Generate a key pair and certificate

documents.t: Sign in to your SAP SuccessFactors instance as an administrator. Search for Manage OAuth2 Client Applications in Admin Center's action search, or navigate to it directly under Admin Center > Company Settings. Choose Register Client Application and provide the following information: Field Description Application Name A name to identify this integration Description An optional description X.509 Certificate The contents of certificate.pem as a single continuous base64 string, with the -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- / -----END CERTIFICATE----- lines and line breaks removed. Produce this with awk '/BEGIN CERTIFICATE/{flag=1;next}/END CERTIFICATE/{flag=0}flag' certificate.pem | tr -d '\n' and paste the single line of output it prints. Choose Register to save the application.
documents.s: Step 2: Register an OAuth2 client application

documents.t: After registering, open the application (choose View from the application list) to find the Company ID and the API Key SAP assigned to it. You now have everything the connector's SAML Bearer configuration needs: the API Key, the Company ID, the username to authenticate as, your private_key.pem and certificate.pem files, and the OAuth2 token endpoint (typically https://<admin-center-host>/oauth/token).

Build an integration that connects to SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central and retrieves FOLegalEntityLocalUSA records through the SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central Foundation Organization connector. The integration exposes an automation entry point that calls the operation and stores the result in a variable you can process further. Operations used: List Fo Legal Entity Local Us As : Queries the FOLegalEntityLocalUSA collection and returns a page of entities, optionally filtered, sorted, and paged through OData query options.
Access to a SAP SuccessFactors OData API server (see the setup guide) A company ID, username, and password, or OAuth 2.0 credentials
New to WSO2 Integrator? Follow the Create a New Integration guide to set up your integration first, then return here to add the connector.
documents.s: Setting up the SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central Foundation Organization integration

documents.t: Select Add Artifact. Select Connection to open the connector search palette.
Enter ecfoundationorganization in the search field. Select the Ecfoundationorganization connector card.
documents.s: Step 2: Select the SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central Foundation Organization connector

documents.t: Bind every required connection field to a configurable variable. Config : Expression containing the auth credentials for the SAP SuccessFactors OData server — bind username to a sfUsername configurable variable and password to a sfPassword configurable variable. Hostname : The SAP SuccessFactors OData API server hostname — bind to a sfHostname configurable variable.
documents.s: Step 3: Bind the connection parameters to configurable variables

documents.t: Select Save Connection and verify that ecfoundationorganizationClient appears in the Connections section.

Select Configurations at the bottom of the project tree under Data Mappers. Enter a value for each configurable listed below before you run the integration. sfUsername (configurable string) : The SAP SuccessFactors login username, formatted as <username>@<companyID>. sfPassword (configurable string) : The SAP SuccessFactors login password. sfHostname (configurable string) : The SAP SuccessFactors OData API server hostname, for example api68sales.successfactors.com.
documents.s: Step 5: Set actual values for your configurables

documents.t: Select Add Artifact. Select Automation. Select Create to accept the default settings.
documents.s: Step 6: Add an automation entry point

documents.t: Select the + icon between Start and Error Handler. Expand ecfoundationorganizationClient to display its operations. Select List Fo Legal Entity Local Us As. The operation has no required parameters, so review the auto-generated result variable. Result : Name of the variable that stores the returned FOLegalEntityLocalUSA records — leave the default value, ecfoundationorganizationWrapper. Select Save. The operation step appears in the automation flow between Start and Error Handler.

SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central is a comprehensive human capital management solution that helps organizations manage their workforce effectively. It provides a unified platform for HR processes including employee data management, organizational structures, and employment lifecycle management. WSO2 SAP Successfactors Foundation Organization provides a way to interact with the SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central APIs.

This guide walks you through getting the necessary details from SAP SuccessFactors so that the connector can authenticate and communicate with your Employee Central instance. This connector supports two authentication methods: Basic Authentication and OAuth 2.0 SAML Bearer.

If you already have a username and password for this integration to work, you can use those directly. If you'd rather create a new account with narrowed scope for this integration, follow these steps: Sign in to your SAP SuccessFactors instance as an administrator. Navigate to Admin Center > Add New Employee and create a new user account for this integration. Navigate to Admin Center > Manage Permission Roles, create a role scoped to only the permissions this integration needs, and grant it to the new user. Navigate to Admin Center > Reset User Password and set a password for the new user account. In either case, you will also need the API server hostname for your SuccessFactors region, for example, api12.successfactors.eu. The complete list of API server hostnames by region is available in the SAP SuccessFactors API documentation.

Generate an RSA key pair and a matching X.509 certificate. If you don't already have one, generate a self-signed pair with OpenSSL: openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout private_key.pem -out certificate.pem -days 365 -nodes -subj "/CN=YourAppName" private_key.pem is secret - it never leaves your machine or gets uploaded anywhere. Only certificate.pem is registered with SAP.
documents.s: Step 1: Generate a key pair and certificate

documents.t: Sign in to your SAP SuccessFactors instance as an administrator. Search for Manage OAuth2 Client Applications in Admin Center's action search, or navigate to it directly under Admin Center > Company Settings. Choose Register Client Application and provide the following information: Field Description Application Name A name to identify this integration Description An optional description X.509 Certificate The contents of certificate.pem as a single continuous base64 string, with the -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- / -----END CERTIFICATE----- lines and line breaks removed. Produce this with awk '/BEGIN CERTIFICATE/{flag=1;next}/END CERTIFICATE/{flag=0}flag' certificate.pem | tr -d '\n' and paste the single line of output it prints. Choose Register to save the application.
documents.s: Step 2: Register an OAuth2 client application

documents.t: After registering, open the application (choose View from the application list) to find the Company ID and the API Key SAP assigned to it. You now have everything the connector's SAML Bearer configuration needs: the API Key, the Company ID, the username to authenticate as, your private_key.pem and certificate.pem files, and the OAuth2 token endpoint (typically https://<admin-center-host>/oauth/token).

Build an integration that connects to SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central and retrieves secondary assignment item records through the SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central Global Assignment connector. The integration exposes an automation entry point that calls the operation and stores the result in a variable you can process further. Operations used: List Secondary Assignments Items : Queries the SecondaryAssignmentsItem collection and returns a page of entities, optionally filtered, sorted, and paged through OData query options.
Access to a SAP SuccessFactors OData API server (see the setup guide) A company ID, username, and password, or OAuth 2.0 credentials
New to WSO2 Integrator? Follow the Create a New Integration guide to set up your integration first, then return here to add the connector.
documents.s: Setting up the SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central Global Assignment integration

documents.t: Select Add Artifact. Select Connection to open the connector search palette.
Enter ecglobalassignment in the search field. Select the Ecglobalassignment connector card.
documents.s: Step 2: Select the SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central Global Assignment connector

documents.t: Bind every required connection field to a configurable variable. Config : Expression containing the auth credentials for the SAP SuccessFactors OData server — bind username to a sfUsername configurable variable and password to a sfPassword configurable variable. Hostname : The SAP SuccessFactors OData API server hostname — bind to a sfHostname configurable variable.
documents.s: Step 3: Bind the connection parameters to configurable variables

documents.t: Select Save Connection and verify that ecglobalassignmentClient appears in the Connections section.

Select Configurations at the bottom of the project tree under Data Mappers. Enter a value for each configurable listed below before you run the integration. sfUsername (configurable string) : The SAP SuccessFactors login username, formatted as <username>@<companyID>. sfPassword (configurable string) : The SAP SuccessFactors login password. sfHostname (configurable string) : The SAP SuccessFactors OData API server hostname, for example api68sales.successfactors.com.
documents.s: Step 5: Set actual values for your configurables

documents.t: Select Add Artifact. Select Automation. Select Create to accept the default settings.
documents.s: Step 6: Add an automation entry point

documents.t: Select the + icon between Start and Error Handler. Expand ecglobalassignmentClient to display its operations. Select List Secondary Assignments Items. The operation has no required parameters, so review the auto-generated result variable. Result : Name of the variable that stores the returned SecondaryAssignmentsItem records — leave the default value, ecglobalassignmentWrapper. Select Save. The operation step appears in the automation flow between Start and Error Handler.

SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central is a comprehensive human capital management solution that helps organizations manage their workforce effectively. It provides a unified platform for HR processes including employee data management, organizational structures, and employment lifecycle management. WSO2 SAP Successfactors Global Assignment provides a way to interact with the SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central APIs.

This guide walks you through getting the necessary details from SAP SuccessFactors so that the connector can authenticate and communicate with your Employee Central instance. This connector supports two authentication methods: Basic Authentication and OAuth 2.0 SAML Bearer.

If you already have a username and password for this integration to work, you can use those directly. If you'd rather create a new account with narrowed scope for this integration, follow these steps: Sign in to your SAP SuccessFactors instance as an administrator. Navigate to Admin Center > Add New Employee and create a new user account for this integration. Navigate to Admin Center > Manage Permission Roles, create a role scoped to only the permissions this integration needs, and grant it to the new user. Navigate to Admin Center > Reset User Password and set a password for the new user account. In either case, you will also need the API server hostname for your SuccessFactors region, for example, api12.successfactors.eu. The complete list of API server hostnames by region is available in the SAP SuccessFactors API documentation.

Generate an RSA key pair and a matching X.509 certificate. If you don't already have one, generate a self-signed pair with OpenSSL: openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout private_key.pem -out certificate.pem -days 365 -nodes -subj "/CN=YourAppName" private_key.pem is secret - it never leaves your machine or gets uploaded anywhere. Only certificate.pem is registered with SAP.
documents.s: Step 1: Generate a key pair and certificate

documents.t: Sign in to your SAP SuccessFactors instance as an administrator. Search for Manage OAuth2 Client Applications in Admin Center's action search, or navigate to it directly under Admin Center > Company Settings. Choose Register Client Application and provide the following information: Field Description Application Name A name to identify this integration Description An optional description X.509 Certificate The contents of certificate.pem as a single continuous base64 string, with the -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- / -----END CERTIFICATE----- lines and line breaks removed. Produce this with awk '/BEGIN CERTIFICATE/{flag=1;next}/END CERTIFICATE/{flag=0}flag' certificate.pem | tr -d '\n' and paste the single line of output it prints. Choose Register to save the application.
documents.s: Step 2: Register an OAuth2 client application

documents.t: After registering, open the application (choose View from the application list) to find the Company ID and the API Key SAP assigned to it. You now have everything the connector's SAML Bearer configuration needs: the API Key, the Company ID, the username to authenticate as, your private_key.pem and certificate.pem files, and the OAuth2 token endpoint (typically https://<admin-center-host>/oauth/token).

Build an integration that connects to SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central and retrieves benefit employee claim records through the SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central Global Benefits connector. The integration exposes an automation entry point that calls the operation and stores the result in a variable you can process further. Operations used: List Benefit Employee Claims : Queries the BenefitEmployeeClaim collection and returns a page of entities, optionally filtered, sorted, and paged through OData query options.
Access to a SAP SuccessFactors OData API server (see the setup guide) A company ID, username, and password, or OAuth 2.0 credentials
New to WSO2 Integrator? Follow the Create a New Integration guide to set up your integration first, then return here to add the connector.
documents.s: Setting up the SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central Global Benefits integration

documents.t: Select Add Artifact. Select Connection to open the connector search palette.
Enter ecglobalbenefits in the search field. Select the Ecglobalbenefits connector card.
documents.s: Step 2: Select the SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central Global Benefits connector

documents.t: Bind every required connection field to a configurable variable. Config : Expression containing the auth credentials for the SAP SuccessFactors OData server — bind username to a sfUsername configurable variable and password to a sfPassword configurable variable. Hostname : The SAP SuccessFactors OData API server hostname — bind to a sfHostname configurable variable.
documents.s: Step 3: Bind the connection parameters to configurable variables

documents.t: Select Save Connection and verify that ecglobalbenefitsClient appears in the Connections section.

Select Configurations at the bottom of the project tree under Data Mappers. Enter a value for each configurable listed below before you run the integration. sfUsername (configurable string) : The SAP SuccessFactors login username, formatted as <username>@<companyID>. sfPassword (configurable string) : The SAP SuccessFactors login password. sfHostname (configurable string) : The SAP SuccessFactors OData API server hostname, for example api68sales.successfactors.com.
documents.s: Step 5: Set actual values for your configurables

documents.t: Select Add Artifact. Select Automation. Select Create to accept the default settings.
documents.s: Step 6: Add an automation entry point

documents.t: Select the + icon between Start and Error Handler. Expand ecglobalbenefitsClient to display its operations. Select List Benefit Employee Claims. The operation has no required parameters, so review the auto-generated result variable. Result : Name of the variable that stores the returned BenefitEmployeeClaim records — leave the default value, jsonResult. Select Save. The operation step appears in the automation flow between Start and Error Handler.
documents.s: Step 7: Expand the connection and configure the List Benefit Employee Claims operation

SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central is a comprehensive human capital management solution that helps organizations manage their workforce effectively. It provides a unified platform for HR processes including employee data management, organizational structures, and employment lifecycle management. WSO2 SAP Successfactors Global Benefits provides a way to interact with the SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central APIs.

This guide walks you through getting the necessary details from SAP SuccessFactors so that the connector can authenticate and communicate with your Employee Central instance. This connector supports two authentication methods: Basic Authentication and OAuth 2.0 SAML Bearer.

If you already have a username and password for this integration to work, you can use those directly. If you'd rather create a new account with narrowed scope for this integration, follow these steps: Sign in to your SAP SuccessFactors instance as an administrator. Navigate to Admin Center > Add New Employee and create a new user account for this integration. Navigate to Admin Center > Manage Permission Roles, create a role scoped to only the permissions this integration needs, and grant it to the new user. Navigate to Admin Center > Reset User Password and set a password for the new user account. In either case, you will also need the API server hostname for your SuccessFactors region, for example, api12.successfactors.eu. The complete list of API server hostnames by region is available in the SAP SuccessFactors API documentation.

Generate an RSA key pair and a matching X.509 certificate. Navigate to Admin Center > Manage Permission Roles, create a role scoped to only the permissions this integration needs, and grant it to the new user. Navigate to Admin Center > Reset User Password and set a password for the new user account. In either case, you will also need the API server hostname for your SuccessFactors region, for example, api12.successfactors.eu. The complete list of API server hostnames by region is available in the SAP SuccessFactors API documentation.

Generate an RSA key pair and a matching X.509 certificate. If you don't already have one, generate a self-signed pair with OpenSSL: openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout private_key.pem -out certificate.pem -days 365 -nodes -subj "/CN=YourAppName" private_key.pem is secret - it never leaves your machine or gets uploaded anywhere. Only certificate.pem is registered with SAP.
documents.s: Step 1: Generate a key pair and certificate

documents.t: Sign in to your SAP SuccessFactors instance as an administrator. Search for Manage OAuth2 Client Applications in Admin Center's action search, or navigate to it directly under Admin Center > Company Settings. Choose Register Client Application and provide the following information: Field Description Application Name A name to identify this integration Description An optional description X.509 Certificate The contents of certificate.pem as a single continuous base64 string, with the -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- / -----END CERTIFICATE----- lines and line breaks removed. Produce this with awk '/BEGIN CERTIFICATE/{flag=1;next}/END CERTIFICATE/{flag=0}flag' certificate.pem | tr -d '\n' and paste the single line of output it prints. Choose Register to save the application.
documents.s: Step 2: Register an OAuth2 client application

documents.t: After registering, open the application (choose View from the application list) to find the Company ID and the API Key SAP assigned to it. You now have everything the connector's SAML Bearer configuration needs: the API Key, the Company ID, the username to authenticate as, your private_key.pem and certificate.pem files, and the OAuth2 token endpoint (typically https://<admin-center-host>/oauth/token).
Action Reference - Available operations

The ballerinax/sap.successfactors.ecpaymentinformation package exposes the following clients: Available clients: Client Purpose Client Manages ecpaymentinformation objects: PaymentInformationDetailV3KEN, PaymentInformationDetailV3ISR, PaymentInformationDetailV3, PaymentInformationDetailV3ARG, PaymentMethodV3, Bank, CustomPayTypeAssignment, CustomPayType…, over the SAP SuccessFactors OData v2 API.
You can use these APIs to maintain the country-dependent fields of payment information details for specific countries.

Build an integration that connects to SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central and retrieves PaymentInformationDetailV3KEN records through the SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central Payment Information connector. The integration exposes an automation entry point that calls the operation and stores the result in a variable you can process further. Operations used: List Payment Information Detail V3ke Ns : Queries the PaymentInformationDetailV3KEN collection and returns a page of entities, optionally filtered, sorted, and paged through OData query options.
Access to a SAP SuccessFactors OData API server (see the setup guide) A company ID, username, and password, or OAuth 2.0 credentials
New to WSO2 Integrator? Follow the Create a New Integration guide to set up your integration first, then return here to add the connector.
documents.s: Setting up the SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central Payment Information integration

documents.t: Select Add Artifact. Select Connection to open the connector search palette.
Enter ecpaymentinformation in the search field. Select the Ecpaymentinformation connector card.
documents.s: Step 2: Select the SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central Payment Information connector

documents.t: Bind every required connection field to a configurable variable. Config : Expression containing the auth credentials for the SAP SuccessFactors OData server — bind username to a sfUsername configurable variable and password to a sfPassword configurable variable. Hostname : The SAP SuccessFactors OData API server hostname — bind to a sfHostname configurable variable.
documents.s: Step 3: Bind the connection parameters to configurable variables

documents.t: Select Save Connection and verify that ecpaymentinformationClient appears in the Connections section.

Select Configurations at the bottom of the project tree under Data Mappers. Enter a value for each configurable listed below before you run the integration. sfUsername (configurable string) : The SAP SuccessFactors login username, formatted as <username>@<companyID>. sfPassword (configurable string) : The SAP SuccessFactors login password. sfHostname (configurable string) : The SAP SuccessFactors OData API server hostname, for example api68sales.successfactors.com.
documents.s: Step 5: Set actual values for your configurables

documents.t: Select Add Artifact. Select Automation. Select Create to accept the default settings.
documents.s: Step 6: Add an automation entry point

documents.t: Select the + icon between Start and Error Handler. Expand ecpaymentinformationClient to display its operations. Select List Payment Information Detail V3ke Ns. The operation has no required parameters, so review the auto-generated result variable. Result : Name of the variable that stores the returned PaymentInformationDetailV3KEN records — leave the default value, ecpaymentinformationWrapper. Select Save. The operation step appears in the automation flow between Start and Error Handler.

This guide walks you through getting the necessary details from SAP SuccessFactors so that the connector can authenticate and communicate with your Employee Central instance. This connector supports two authentication methods: Basic Authentication and OAuth 2.0 SAML Bearer.

If you already have a username and password for this integration to work, you can use those directly. If you'd rather create a new account with narrowed scope for this integration, follow these steps: Sign in to your SAP SuccessFactors instance as an administrator. Navigate to Admin Center > Add New Employee and create a new user account for this integration. Navigate to Admin Center > Manage Permission Roles, create a role scoped to only the permissions this integration needs, and grant it to the new user. Navigate to Admin Center > Reset User Password and set a password for the new user account. In either case, you will also need the API server hostname for your SuccessFactors region, for example, api12.successfactors.eu. The complete list of API server hostnames by region is available in the SAP SuccessFactors API documentation.

Generate an RSA key pair and a matching X.509 certificate. If you don't already have one, generate a self-signed pair with OpenSSL: openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout private_key.pem -out certificate.pem -days 365 -nodes -subj "/CN=YourAppName" private_key.pem is secret - it never leaves your machine or gets uploaded anywhere. Only certificate.pem is registered with SAP.
documents.s: Step 1: Generate a key pair and certificate

documents.t: Sign in to your SAP SuccessFactors instance as an administrator. Search for Manage OAuth2 Client Applications in Admin Center's action search, or navigate to it directly under Admin Center > Company Settings. Choose Register Client Application and provide the following information: Field Description Application Name A name to identify this integration Description An optional description X.509 Certificate The contents of certificate.pem as a single continuous base64 string, with the -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- / -----END CERTIFICATE----- lines and line breaks removed. Produce this with awk '/BEGIN CERTIFICATE/{flag=1;next}/END CERTIFICATE/{flag=0}flag' certificate.pem | tr -d '\n' and paste the single line of output it prints. Choose Register to save the application.
documents.s: Step 2: Register an OAuth2 client application

documents.t: After registering, open the application (choose View from the application list) to find the Company ID and the API Key SAP assigned to it. You now have everything the connector's SAML Bearer configuration needs: the API Key, the Company ID, the username to authenticate as, your private_key.pem and certificate.pem files, and the OAuth2 token endpoint (typically https://<admin-center-host>/oauth/token).

Build an integration that connects to SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central and retrieves employee time sheet records through the SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central Payroll Time Sheets connector. The integration exposes an automation entry point that calls the operation and stores the result in a variable you can process further. Operations used: List Employee Time Sheets : Queries the EmployeeTimeSheet collection and returns a page of entities, optionally filtered, sorted, and paged through OData query options.
Access to a SAP SuccessFactors OData API server (see the setup guide) A company ID, username, and password, or OAuth 2.0 credentials
New to WSO2 Integrator? Follow the Create a New Integration guide to set up your integration first, then return here to add the connector.
documents.s: Setting up the SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central Payroll Time Sheets integration

documents.t: Select Add Artifact. Select Connection to open the connector search palette.
Enter ecpayrolltimesheets in the search field. Select the Ecpayrolltimesheets connector card.
documents.s: Step 2: Select the SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central Payroll Time Sheets connector

documents.t: Bind every required connection field to a configurable variable. Config : Expression containing the auth credentials for the SAP SuccessFactors OData server — bind username to a sfUsername configurable variable and password to a sfPassword configurable variable. Hostname : The SAP SuccessFactors OData API server hostname — bind to a sfHostname configurable variable.
documents.s: Step 3: Bind the connection parameters to configurable variables

documents.t: Select Save Connection and verify that ecpayrolltimesheetsClient appears in the Connections section.

Select Configurations at the bottom of the project tree under Data Mappers. Enter a value for each configurable listed below before you run the integration. sfUsername (configurable string) : The SAP SuccessFactors login username, formatted as <username>@<companyID>. sfPassword (configurable string) : The SAP SuccessFactors login password. sfHostname (configurable string) : The SAP SuccessFactors OData API server hostname, for example api68sales.successfactors.com.
documents.s: Step 5: Set actual values for your configurables

documents.t: Select Add Artifact. Select Automation. Select Create to accept the default settings.

documents.t: Select the + icon between Start and Error Handler. Expand ecpayrolltimesheetsClient to display its operations. Select List Employee Time Sheets. The operation has no required parameters, so review the auto-generated result variable. Result : Name of the variable that stores the returned EmployeeTimeSheet records — leave the default value, ecpayrolltimesheetsWrapper. Select Save. The operation step appears in the automation flow between Start and Error Handler.

SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central is a comprehensive human capital management solution that helps organizations manage their workforce effectively. It provides a unified platform for HR processes including employee data management, organizational structures, and employment lifecycle management. WSO2 SAP Successfactors Payroll Time Sheets provides a way to interact with the SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central APIs. The service allows to manage employee time sheet data, working hours, and payroll-related time information.

This guide walks you through getting the necessary details from SAP SuccessFactors so that the connector can authenticate and communicate with your Employee Central instance. This connector supports two authentication methods: Basic Authentication and OAuth 2.0 SAML Bearer.

If you already have a username and password for this integration to work, you can use those directly. If you'd rather create a new account with narrowed scope for this integration, follow these steps: Sign in to your SAP SuccessFactors instance as an administrator. Navigate to Admin Center > Add New Employee and create a new user account for this integration. Navigate to Admin Center > Manage Permission Roles, create a role scoped to only the permissions this integration needs, and grant it to the new user. Navigate to Admin Center > Reset User Password and set a password for the new user account. In either case, you will also need the API server hostname for your SuccessFactors region, for example, api12.successfactors.eu. The complete list of API server hostnames by region is available in the SAP SuccessFactors API documentation.

Generate an RSA key pair and a matching X.509 certificate. If you don't already have one, generate a self-signed pair with OpenSSL: openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout private_key.pem -out certificate.pem -days 365 -nodes -subj "/CN=YourAppName" private_key.pem is secret - it never leaves your machine or gets uploaded anywhere. Only certificate.pem is registered with SAP.
documents.s: Step 1: Generate a key pair and certificate

documents.t: Sign in to your SAP SuccessFactors instance as an administrator. Search for Manage OAuth2 Client Applications in Admin Center's action search, or navigate to it directly under Admin Center > Company Settings. Choose Register Client Application and provide the following information: Field Description Application Name A name to identify this integration Description An optional description X.509 Certificate The contents of certificate.pem as a single continuous base64 string, with the -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- / -----END CERTIFICATE----- lines and line breaks removed. Produce this with awk '/BEGIN CERTIFICATE/{flag=1;next}/END CERTIFICATE/{flag=0}flag' certificate.pem | tr -d '\n' and paste the single line of output it prints. Choose Register to save the application.
documents.s: Step 2: Register an OAuth2 client application

documents.t: After registering, open the application (choose View from the application list) to find the Company ID and the API Key SAP assigned to it. You now have everything the connector's SAML Bearer configuration needs: the API Key, the Company ID, the username to authenticate as, your private_key.pem and certificate.pem files, and the OAuth2 token endpoint (typically https://<admin-center-host>/oauth/token).

documents.t: Bind every required connection field to a configurable variable. Config : Expression containing the auth credentials for the SAP SuccessFactors OData server — bind username to a sfUsername configurable variable and password to a sfPassword configurable variable. Hostname : The SAP SuccessFactors OData API server hostname — bind to a sfHostname configurable variable.
documents.s: Step 3: Bind the connection parameters to configurable variables

documents.t: Select Save Connection and verify that ecpersonalinformationClient appears in the Connections section.

Select Configurations at the bottom of the project tree under Data Mappers. Enter a value for each configurable listed below before you run the integration. sfUsername (configurable string) : The SAP SuccessFactors login username, formatted as <username>@<companyID>. sfPassword (configurable string) : The SAP SuccessFactors login password. sfHostname (configurable string) : The SAP SuccessFactors OData API server hostname, for example api68sales.successfactors.com.
documents.s: Step 5: Set actual values for your configurables

documents.t: Select Add Artifact. Select Automation. Select Create to accept the default settings.
documents.s: Step 6: Add an automation entry point

documents.t: Select the + icon between Start and Error Handler. Expand ecpersonalinformationClient to display its operations. Select List Per Emergency Contactss. The operation has no required parameters, so review the auto-generated result variable. Result : Name of the variable that stores the returned PerEmergencyContacts records — leave the default value, ecpersonalinformationWrapper. Select Save. The operation step appears in the automation flow between Start and Error Handler.

SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central is a comprehensive human capital management solution that helps organizations manage their workforce effectively. It provides a unified platform for HR processes including employee data management, organizational structures, and employment lifecycle management. WSO2 SAP Successfactors Personal Information provides a way to interact with the SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central APIs.

This guide walks you through getting the necessary details from SAP SuccessFactors so that the connector can authenticate and communicate with your Employee Central instance. This connector supports two authentication methods: Basic Authentication and OAuth 2.0 SAML Bearer.

If you already have a username and password for this integration to work, you can use those directly. If you'd rather create a new account with narrowed scope for this integration, follow these steps: Sign in to your SAP SuccessFactors instance as an administrator. Navigate to Admin Center > Add New Employee and create a new user account for this integration. Navigate to Admin Center > Manage Permission Roles, create a role scoped to only the permissions this integration needs, and grant it to the new user. Navigate to Admin Center > Reset User Password and set a password for the new user account. In either case, you will also need the API server hostname for your SuccessFactors region, for example, api12.successfactors.eu. The complete list of API server hostnames by region is available in the SAP SuccessFactors API documentation.

Generate an RSA key pair and a matching X.509 certificate. If you don't already have one, generate a self-signed pair with OpenSSL: openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout private_key.pem -out certificate.pem -days 365 -nodes -subj "/CN=YourAppName" private_key.pem is secret - it never leaves your machine or gets uploaded anywhere. Only certificate.pem is registered with SAP.
documents.s: Step 1: Generate a key pair and certificate

documents.t: Sign in to your SAP SuccessFactors instance as an administrator. Search for Manage OAuth2 Client Applications in Admin Center's action search, or navigate to it directly under Admin Center > Company Settings. Choose Register Client Application and provide the following information: Field Description Application Name A name to identify this integration Description An optional description X.509 Certificate The contents of certificate.pem as a single continuous base64 string, with the -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- / -----END CERTIFICATE----- lines and line breaks removed. Produce this with awk '/BEGIN CERTIFICATE/{flag=1;next}/END CERTIFICATE/{flag=0}flag' certificate.pem | tr -d '\n' and paste the single line of output it prints. Choose Register to save the application.
documents.s: Step 2: Register an OAuth2 client application

documents.t: After registering, open the application (choose View from the application list) to find the Company ID and the API Key SAP assigned to it. You now have everything the connector's SAML Bearer configuration needs: the API Key, the Company ID, the username to authenticate as, your private_key.pem and certificate.pem files, and the OAuth2 token endpoint (typically https://<admin-center-host>/oauth/token).

Enter ecpositionmanagement in the search field. Select the Ecpositionmanagement connector card.
documents.s: Step 2: Select the SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central Position Management connector

documents.t: Bind every required connection field to a configurable variable. Config : Expression containing the auth credentials for the SAP SuccessFactors OData server — bind username to a sfUsername configurable variable and password to a sfPassword configurable variable. Hostname : The SAP SuccessFactors OData API server hostname — bind to a sfHostname configurable variable.
documents.s: Step 3: Bind the connection parameters to configurable variables

documents.t: Select Save Connection and verify that ecpositionmanagementClient appears in the Connections section.

Select Configurations at the bottom of the project tree under Data Mappers. Enter a value for each configurable listed below before you run the integration. sfUsername (configurable string) : The SAP SuccessFactors login username, formatted as <username>@<companyID>. sfPassword (configurable string) : The SAP SuccessFactors login password. sfHostname (configurable string) : The SAP SuccessFactors OData API server hostname, for example api68sales.successfactors.com.
documents.s: Step 5: Set actual values for your configurables

documents.t: Select Add Artifact. Select Automation. Select Create to accept the default settings.
documents.s: Step 6: Add an automation entry point

documents.t: Select the + icon between Start and Error Handler. Expand ecpositionmanagementClient to display its operations. Select List Position Requisition Statuses. The operation has no required parameters, so review the auto-generated result variable. Result : Name of the variable that stores the returned PositionRequisitionStatus records — leave the default value, ecpositionmanagementWrapper. Select Save. The operation step appears in the automation flow between Start and Error Handler.

The SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central connectors provide practical examples illustrating usage in various scenarios. Explore these examples, covering use cases like syncing employee data and sending notifications. Google Sheets to SuccessFactors : Read employee records from a Google Sheets roster and create Personal Information records in SuccessFactors. SuccessFactors to Slack : Poll SuccessFactors for newly onboarded employees and send welcome notifications to a Slack channel.

SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central is a comprehensive human capital management solution that helps organizations manage their workforce effectively. It provides a unified platform for HR processes including employee data management, organizational structures, and employment lifecycle management. WSO2 SAP Successfactors Position Management provides a way to interact with the SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central APIs. The service allows to manage organizational positions, position hierarchies, and position-related information.

This guide walks you through getting the necessary details from SAP SuccessFactors so that the connector can authenticate and communicate with your Employee Central instance. This connector supports two authentication methods: Basic Authentication and OAuth 2.0 SAML Bearer.

If you already have a username and password for this integration to work, you can use those directly. If you'd rather create a new account with narrowed scope for this integration, follow these steps: Sign in to your SAP SuccessFactors instance as an administrator. Navigate to Admin Center > Add New Employee and create a new user account for this integration. Navigate to Admin Center > Manage Permission Roles, create a role scoped to only the permissions this integration needs, and grant it to the new user. Navigate to Admin Center > Reset User Password and set a password for the new user account. In either case, you will also need the API server hostname for your SuccessFactors region, for example, api12.successfactors.eu. The complete list of API server hostnames by region is available in the SAP SuccessFactors API documentation.

Generate an RSA key pair and a matching X.509 certificate. If you don't already have one, generate a self-signed pair with OpenSSL: openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout private_key.pem -out certificate.pem -days 365 -nodes -subj "/CN=YourAppName" private_key.pem is secret - it never leaves your machine or gets uploaded anywhere. Only certificate.pem is registered with SAP.
documents.s: Step 1: Generate a key pair and certificate

documents.t: Sign in to your SAP SuccessFactors instance as an administrator. Search for Manage OAuth2 Client Applications in Admin Center's action search, or navigate to it directly under Admin Center > Company Settings. Choose Register Client Application and provide the following information: Field Description Application Name A name to identify this integration Description An optional description X.509 Certificate The contents of certificate.pem as a single continuous base64 string, with the -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- / -----END CERTIFICATE----- lines and line breaks removed. Produce this with awk '/BEGIN CERTIFICATE/{flag=1;next}/END CERTIFICATE/{flag=0}flag' certificate.pem | tr -d '\n' and paste the single line of output it prints. Choose Register to save the application.
documents.s: Step 2: Register an OAuth2 client application

documents.t: After registering, open the application (choose View from the application list) to find the Company ID and the API Key SAP assigned to it. You now have everything the connector's SAML Bearer configuration needs: the API Key, the Company ID, the username to authenticate as, your private_key.pem and certificate.pem files, and the OAuth2 token endpoint (typically https://<admin-center-host>/oauth/token).

The ballerinax/sap.successfactors.ecskillsmanagement package exposes the following clients: Available clients: Client Purpose Client Manages ecskillsmanagement objects: CertificationContent, FamilyEntity, CertificationEntity, JobResponsibilityContent, InterviewQuestionContent, JobResponsibilityEntity, RatedSkillMapping, RoleCompetencyBehaviorMappingEntity…, over the SAP SuccessFactors OData v2 API.
You can use these APIs to manage the information about employees skills.

ConnectionConfig​ Provides a set of configurations for controlling the behaviours when communicating with the SAP SuccessFactors OData endpoint. Passed as the argument to the client initializer. Field Type Default Description auth http:CredentialsConfig Required Configurations related to client authentication httpVersion http:HttpVersion See default The HTTP version understood by the client http1Settings http:ClientHttp1Settings See default Configurations related to HTTP/1.x protocol http2Settings http:ClientHttp2Settings See default Configurations related to HTTP/2 protocol timeout decimal See default The maximum time to wait (in seconds) for a response before closing the connection forwarded string See default The choice of setting forwarded/x-forwarded header followRedirects http:FollowRedirects Optional Configurations associated with Redirection poolConfig http:PoolConfiguration Optional Configurations associated with request pooling cache http:CacheConfig See default HTTP caching related configurations compression http:Compression See default Specifies the way of handling compression (accept-encoding) header circuitBreaker http:CircuitBreakerConfig Optional Configurations associated with the behaviour of the Circuit Breaker retryConfig http:RetryConfig Optional Configurations associated with retrying cookieConfig http:CookieConfig Optional Configurations associated with cookies responseLimits http:ResponseLimitConfigs See default Configurations associated with inbound response size limits secureSocket http:ClientSecureSocket Optional SSL/TLS-related options proxy http:ProxyConfig Optional Proxy server related options socketConfig http:ClientSocketConfig See default Provides settings related to client socket configuration validation boolean See default Enables the inbound payload validation functionality which provided by the constraint package. Enabled by default laxDataBinding boolean See default Enables relaxed data binding on the client side. When enabled, nil values are treated as optional, and absent fields are handled as nilable types. Enabled by default. The client also accepts a hostname string parameter (the SAP SuccessFactors API server host) and an optional port (defaults to 443).
